correctness.rationale: Binet quartic identities yield exactly 5 modes 1,rho±1,rho±2 where rho=−alpha² has monic quadratic t²+3t+1. Window-sum sequences obey an integer fifth-order recurrence with invertible constant term, reducing their all-translation gcd to five initial windows. For each p≥7, distinct modes and unit coefficients give invertible Vandermonde modulo p^e; all windows vanish iff p^e|k and rho^k=1 modulo p^e. Mod-p order r_p divides k as necessary and p-adic binomial lifting makes it sufficient through valuation ν_p(k). For p=3, nonzero-index fourth-power indicators have period 4, so odd k cannot annihilate every window; p=5 excluded by 5∤k and the mod5 residue indicators; p=2 yields exactly one factor iff 3|k for odd k. Independent integers and finite-algebra modular-order checker verified 80 odd k<200 (5∤k) for both sequences, comparing the first five exact windows; recurrence proves those five exhaust translations, and primewise argument proves all odd permitted lengths.
residual_risks: The discriminant prime 5 and even k are deliberately excluded and should not be extrapolated.

value.rationale: The all-translation gcd is a motivated recurrence-sequence arithmetic invariant, and this exact prime-order rule simultaneously handles two distinct quartic sequences for every odd k coprime to five. It directly addresses a higher-power gap posed after the square case rather than a single small numerical computation.
residual_risks: General recurrence-sequence resultant/divisibility literature under a different formulation might implicitly yield the same local factorization.

final_claim: For each odd k≥1 with 5∤k, the translated consecutive quartic Fibonacci and Lucas window GCDs coincide and equal 2^{1_{3|k}}∏_{p|k,p≥7,r_p|k}p^{ν_p(k)}.
limitations: Only odd lengths with 5∤k; p=5/even-length factorization is not established.
Finite integer/modular testing of 80 window lengths corroborates but does not replace the p-adic proof.
